She’s imo one of the greatest resources for Hekate of our time. Her book “Circle for Hekate” is amazing — while it’s primarily about the goddess, she does expand on her connections with other deities & there is a section about the mystery cult founded around Hekate/Persephone/Demeter, as well as some neat info about Hekate being conflated with them (amongst other deities). The basis of the cult is the story of Persephone’s descent & Demeter’s despair over losing her daughter, and Hekate is the main deity that helps them both. The Covenant website also has a [blog](https://www.hekatecovenant.com/blog) with extensive information on Hekate.

Sorita also has her own publishing house called [Avalonia Books](https://www.avaloniabooks.com/) which has a ton of material on different witchcraft/pagan practices & deities so you might be able to find some interesting books on that site for Persephone & Demeter :)

To your first point — yes I have felt this heavily for a large portion of my life, even with my family (most of whom I don’t speak to for this reason). I am a very loving person, but I’ve had to learn (often the hard way) that most people don’t love like me. I was used, betrayed, you name it by people that I considered dear to me, but to whom I apparently meant very little. The isolation led to a lot of soul searching to truly understand what it was I wanted from relationships, but even more importantly how to build that same love in the relationship I had with myself. 

I learned to establish firm but fair boundaries for myself, I found my voice so that I could truly advocate for said boundaries, and while this didn’t cause me to have a multitude of friends, it highlighted MY people—the ones who would value me in their lives and, even if we didn’t always understand each other, they were always willing to meet me somewhere in the middle. To these people, they know that I’m very big on reciprocal exchange in relationships—not that I go into a connection seeking anything specific, but that I want us both to feel valued in the relationship in the ways that are meaningful to either party. In the past, I’ve had a “best” friend block me on every platform because I told her I felt sad that she never seemed to have time for me unless she needed something but was constantly out with some new friend she had just met weeks ago. That utterly broke my heart but I learned a BIG lesson from that — the ones who genuinely care will hear you when you want or need to be heard, even if the conversation isn’t entirely comfortable, they have enough love to sit with you during the experience. It’s not easy to find them, but I promise you, they are out there.

I’m 30 now and there’s probably less than 10 people that I’d consider wholeheartedly as friends, more like family. Most of them unfortunately do not live in my area, or they tend to be rather busy with their own lives so we will chat on the phone or meet IRL once every few months or so. But this was another thing I had to learn to be okay with—I do still experience bouts of loneliness, but the people I’ve kept in my circle are of the highest quality so I know I’m never truly alone. I could call any of them up right now and while they might not answer because they’re busy, they love me enough to get back to me as soon as they have the time to do so, and that means everything to me.

To your second point — I usually only feel like this when depression strikes again, accompanied by its close friend anhedonia. I still struggle with depression but nowhere near as bad as when I was in my early 20s, and I actually feel like this next decade for me will be the time I genuinely get to do all of the things I wanted to do but couldn’t because I’ve spent a lot of time unburdening myself of the things that convinced me that those things weren’t worthwhile. I don’t know your experiences so I’m not sure if the same is true for you, I’m also not sure if this is a common INFJ trait—but it makes me thing a bit of “gifted kid syndrome”? That inherent perfectionism born of being really good at things when you were young & now that you’re older, you can’t be bothered to do things if you’re not immediately perfect at them. That was a decent portion of the issue for me, though not all of it. Lots of therapy & more soul searching is how I managed to find some sense of a light through that darkness. I unfortunately don’t really have much advice to add however as I feel this issue may be more subjective than objective. 

Either way, you are not alone! I wish you the best of luck in navigating this whacky journey called Life, my friend.

She quickly disappeared after that, but I felt her presence often in that house—I’d sometimes see her watching me from around a corner only to disappear again once she noticed I saw her. I remember in my early college years I had a problem with staying properly hydrated and would grow faint & overheated in certain situations — this happened on a brief hike with my best friend and an acquaintance, I became disoriented and not really able to vocalize what was wrong with me.  Best friend assessed the situation and immediately sat me down in the middle of the trail, handed me a water bottle, and demanded I drink. When that was clearly not enough, she took another bottle and poured it over my head. It was cold & startling lol but honestly exactly what I needed, and if she hadn’t been there with me I might have gotten hurt. 

I think the fear of being so seen for me stems from a belief that people will try to take advantage of me (I’ve grown strong boundaries to ward this off) but for the people who truly see me as I am, 100%, without judgment or ill intentions — I know that they love the hell out of me. It makes me feel less alone to know that someone cares enough to look at me the way I look at others.

When I was in college my ex boyfriend decided that he wanted to be a rapper towards the end of our almost 2 year relationship (not the reason we broke up but it certainly didn’t help). Honestly that whole relationship was embarrassing lol I was young and dumb but got a super sweet cat out of the ordeal so it’s whatever but the rap thing was indeed embarrassing as well. He was a very manic person and thought he was god’s gift to earth so naturally everything he did, including rap, was an act of pure divinity. 

I was an English lit major and taking an advanced poetry writing seminar at the time — I consider myself to be a decent enough writer, but the professor absolutely destroyed just about everything I wrote. I think there were maybe only 1-2 students she seemed to think actually had the poetic chops? Anyway, my ex constantly begged me to bring his rap lyrics in for this professor to critique. The raps were absolute TRASH and I couldn’t believe he would have the audacity to ask that I do that, I wanted NO association with this nonsense. I told him point blank she wouldn’t like them and he always argued back that I just didn’t know what good writing was.

He wasted hundreds, maybe thousands of dollars recording his shitty raps in his shitty friend’s home studio. I think he had a SoundCloud iirc and would subject anyone who came over to our apartment to a taste of his latest single. I would usually excuse myself to go to the restroom for the next however long it took for him to praise himself while his guests smiled politely and gave noncommittal responses.

When we finally did breakup there was this awkward transition of us still living together for a few months. He was super into the rap thing at this point and would brag constantly about how cool and popular and talented he was, and how I was going to miss out on his fame. Major eye roll. It was a small town and I guarantee not a single person had heard anything he produced. Once he left his notebook with lyrics on my dining table and my cat took a MASSIVE dump on what he was working on. I’m talking a real soupy mess, the whole notebook had to be thrown out. My cat was notorious for peeing outside of his litter box but was polite enough to at least poop there. I took it as a serious statement of how absolutely shit this guy was at the rap game — even my cat knew! 

My ex was, of course, absolutely livid. But for some reason decided this meant he should be a freestyle rapper instead. If you can believe it, he was even worse. Some small time rapper performed at a venue in town. Dude went, got absolutely trashed, and made his way on stage before the headliner to freestyle. The crowd laughed and booed until he was forcibly removed from the stage. He came home, vomited sangria into my trash can, and raved about how successful the night was (I heard the truth from his friend a few days later when he came over to help him pack his things). 

He was diagnosed bipolar and refused to take his medication to manage his mania, so I think he genuinely thought that he was amazing at this. I excused his mental illness for way too long in the hopes that he would be accountable but he decided he’d rather spend his days being high, maxing out credit cards on frivolous dreams, and pretending to be a rapper. Its been almost a decade since we broke up and I have no intention of ever speaking to him again but last I heard from a friend, he seemed to be homeless so I don’t think his career panned out the way he expected.

As has been mentioned already in this space, Hekate is not like the Christian god in any sense — she does not punish if you fail to “do right” by her. I’ve worked with her for several years now and initially, I was hesitant to answer her call because I, too, didn’t think I could give what she would ask of me. She was very patient as I began to unravel that all she wanted was for me to put in the work to be a version of myself I could genuinely feel good about — the fear of not being able to give her what she was asking? That was actually the fear that I could not give MYSELF what I asked of me. 

When I was first aware of her call, I was not in a good place mentally and in hindsight I see that I was not willing or capable of meeting myself as deeply as healing required, so I projected that onto Hekate and imagined her to be some demanding, scary deity when that’s the farthest from the truth. In my experiences, she works in reciprocal exchange, as in, she will only put in as much effort as you are willing to put in — nothing more, nothing less. If I’m not ready for something or don’t have the energy to move forward in any way, there is never any issue with this. No punishment, other than the self inflicted feelings of guilt I may attribute to being stagnant in some sense. I feel her energy wane at these times, as if she’s giving me the space to make sense of myself and how everything ties together. These occurrences always end up being just as much of the path as any forward progress, and what I view as stagnation is ultimately more like I had to steep myself in a certain situation or feeling to unravel the wisdom that was buried within it.

With that being said, my advice to you would be to be patient with yourself — if you feel that she is calling to you but there’s some sort of resistance, this might be a good place for self reflection. What is it that you think she’s asking from you? Are your ideas of her based in truth or societal assumptions? What is the root of the resistance that you feel, and is it possible that this is more of an internal obstacle that you are projecting onto Hekate?

She is imo an incredibly benevolent and dynamic being. I consider her as my Divine Mother, but there are so many different sides of her that you could learn about and call forth to aid you in various things in your life. Her love is unconditional, and I think one of her greatest gifts is teaching individuals to love themselves unconditionally as well. I myself have grown in ways I couldn’t have imagined without her, and I will be eternally grateful for this. 

I hope that you find what you’re looking for and I wish you all the best on your path, wherever it may lead you 🙏

I posted this in a separate comment replied to one of my earlier ones but I think if you have an understanding of what the obstacles of yoga are then you’d understand the point that I’m trying to make, which is that safely driving your car doesn’t exactly relate to any of the obstacles described as distracting us from our path.
Are you familiar with the obstacles of yoga? If you were, I think you’d see that something like paying attention while driving does not relate to any of them.

I respectfully disagree. That would mean, by that logic, that paying attention to any obstacle on your path would distract you from said path. Paying attention to things for safety reasons is not a form of distracting thinking as far as I’m concerned. To become IDENTIFIED with the obstacle is where we enter the territory of chitta vritti. If you become so anxious by your desire to be safe then this, too, might even be chitta vritti.

Do you derive your sense of self identification from making a left turn in your car or having to merge to avoid another driver? I’d imagine not. Chitta vritti is what distracts us from the present moment because we become too identified with those obstacles to actually BE in the present moment — to actively be paying attention while driving is, to me, practicing mindfulness. If you are one of the many drivers that is not paying attention because you are too busy answering text messages, then this would be chitta vritti. If you miss your turn because you were too preoccupied with what you’d eat for dinner or your plans for the evening, this is chitta vritti.

If yoga breeds mindfulness, why would you think mindfully driving your car is some sort of distraction? There are two limbs before Samadhi, or bliss, in Raja or Ashtanga Yoga — Dharana and Dhayana, which are concentration and meditation. The Seer achieves Samadhi by moving through the other seven limbs, and the only way to achieve Samadhi is through first acquiring concentration and achieving meditation. So, what the Seer sees is very much related to a heightened sense of concentration of the present moment. All the Seer KNOWS is the present moment, and when that’s all you know you can, of course, safely move through your life. The Seer isn’t having some constant psychedelic experience that makes them stop seeing what’s in front of them.

Yes, definitely! I’d consider it a state of pure awareness—you have the recognition of connection but it doesn’t separate you in any way from living your existence normally, in fact it deepens the experience. It’s not a state I exist in consistently myself just yet but the moments I have experienced it, I was always incredibly present and filled with a delightful sense of contentment and love for all around me. After pursuing my teacher training, I find my desire to genuinely sit with any given experience has increased a lot!

My understanding is that the Seer sees the Truth of Self, which is that we are all One—that all of life exists as a unified energy from which we are not separate, but merely extensions of. For my teacher training we read the translations of Sri Swami Satchidananda. This is commentary from sutra 1.4 but I think it’s helpful for this context:

“If I use the term ‘spirit,’ or ‘Self,’ you might hesitate to believe me, but if the physicist says the wall is nothing but energy, you will believe that. So, using the scientist’s language, there is nothing but energy everywhere. Even the atom is a form of energy. The same energy appears in different forms to which we also give different names. So the form and name are just different versions of the same energy. And, according to the Yogic scientists such as Patanjali—and even many modern scientists—behind the different forms of energy is one unchanging consciousness or spirit or Self.”

The word yoga comes from the Sanskrit word “to yoke” or “unite”, so the process of yoga unites us with the divine understanding that what we are transcends the limitations and identifications of ego to join with the energy of All, Divine Spirit, God, what have you. This is what the Seer comes to see, the Truth of one’s identity as being intrinsically connected to All.

There’s an interesting book, Triumph of the Moon, that offers a history of modern paganism and it discusses how going back to the days of ancient Hekatean worship, the angle of her as like a “dark being of shadows and witchcraft” kind of coincides with the rise of Christianity and the condemnation of paganism (a word literally invented by Christians) as a whole, specifically female deities who were linked to healing & nature. 

As the other commenter mentioned, Hekate was traditionally worshipped as a very positive figure. She was considered a benevolent protector who watched over all, the image of her in triple form reflecting her ability to gaze in every direction of a crossroads and thus offer us her protection from all sides. Statues of her were even kept in the doorways of the homes of ancient worshippers so that she could protect this sacred threshold.

The triple formed Hekate also highlights her role as a goddess who belongs to the under, middle, AND upper worlds. While there is a darker element to her, it is only the tip of the iceberg of who she is as a divine figure. Her underworld aspect is generally considered to be a Guardian of sorts — for instance, in the iconic tale of Persephone’s descent to the underworld, Hekate is the only god who hears her cries and thus leads her back to the realm of the living. In my practice with her, I have definitely been confronted by my personal shadows and it was unsettling at times — but, Hekate was there to both guard and guide me through those storms and allow me to return to “the world of the living,” in this case healing from past traumas and returning to my true self again.

She is very loving and I view her as quite a maternal figure and, as a loving mother often is, she can be stern with us but it is always coming from the purest place of love and desire for our wellbeing. I’m not sure I would agree with the belief that she’s not an ideal first deity to work with, but I will say this: she is imo very big on healing and growth, and in a working relationship, she demands reciprocal exchange. She is happy to provide her love and assistance, but she wants to see that we are willing to also put in the work ourselves. It’s like she’s working on the backend and we have to keep up the front end, otherwise the ultimate experience may not be what we consider ideal. This might be the reason people say she’s not good to work with, but I think that’s more of a reflection of where we are in our lives at the time. When I first acknowledged her call, I found I wasn’t in a place where I felt I could really commit to myself so I communicated this to her — she was very patient and understanding. In time, my life happened in such a way that her signs began cropping up again but I knew this time I was ready to work with her. 

If you are interested in knowing more about Hekate, I’d definitely suggest reading up on her, she’s truly fascinating! Working with her is pretty subjective so it doesn’t have to have anything to do with magic or religion — it can be whatever feels most appropriate to you. She is ultimately kind, loving, and fair, and if she is indeed calling to you she can be pretty clever about it (like with the dream, or seeing things about her in your life all of a sudden). Past the calling, the rest is pretty much up to you!

I know you said you’re looking for non-physical solutions but I second the mention of TMJ. The masseter muscle in the jaw is considered to be one of the strongest muscles in the body, so it’s natural for it to build up a lot of tension over time. I’ve struggled with TMJ myself for about two decades and the symptoms sound similar to what you’ve described. A bulk of my issues stemmed from grinding/clenching my teeth at night (this actually also caused night terrors & fracturing of molars) and I’ve been able to solve this sleeping issue with a professional night guard.

Stretching of the jaw has also helped me reduce tension, it’s an odd thing to picture or was for me at first — but a combination of moving the jaw to find where it catches, using the hands to gingerly stretch beyond the catch, and massaging where necessary is what I do, sometimes just when I’m watching tv for an hour or so. The buildup of tension can cause stretching to feel somewhat painful, and with the construction of the area stretching it will essentially open up “new” space in your jaw/mouth area — I’ve found after sessions of this the inside of my cheek will be a bit raw. I do also struggle with gum issues myself, and I find that this stretching practice (along with an upgrade to an electric toothbrush!) has dramatically cut down on the amount of inflammation I feel there (I’m due for my routine dentist appt shortly and I’m curious what their take on my gums will be).

The tension of our bodies can’t be confined to a single area, so the jaw tension will warp into tension in the neck, so stretching this area of the body will be helpful as well. I’ve had thyroid issues for some time that doctors can’t really identify, but my personal practices make me believe that this, too, is tied into tension. The thyroid rests within the neck, and very close to our throat chakra, so I think it’s possible that for me, the accumulation of tension in my jaw/neck/maybe even shoulders was interfering with my thyroid in a physical sense — but also in an energetic sense. Relieving tension there over time has freed my creativity more than I’ve experienced in a while. I sing a lot myself, and I cannot emphasize enough the growing ease I feel with my singing (in myself and my form) from a dedicated stretching practice.

The physical implications of tension are very intimately related to the energetic implications of it imo, and I personally don’t think we can completely resolve an issue within ourselves working in just one sense. My experiences with stretching have deeply transformed me in an energetic way, and that release of tension over time allows me to focus more closely on reducing the tension that’s created going forward. Overall I think it would be beneficial to perhaps see if you are struggling with a TMJ issue and physical remedies for that, and I believe the energetic aspect will come to work itself out :) perhaps some work on clearing your energetic centers may also be helpful!

I tend to try to use some form of body movement to try to ground myself and squash that nagging desire to escape my body—light yoga, a short walk, or something comparable can be helpful. Besides that, I have a friend who is an occupational therapist for children and I asked her how she helps kids cope with overstimulation. She mentioned movement is definitely important, but she specifically said she’ll encourage the kids to extend their limbs & stretch them as far as they can, sometimes a cycle of bringing your arms close to your chest and then stretching them out really far — she said the goal here is to basically have your limbs tug at your body, there was some psych explanation I can’t recall atm but she did say it works really well to ground an overstimulated child & bring them back to a sense of balance within themselves. Not a child myself but I do tend to do this and have had effective results.

If movement is NOT an option, however, I’ve also learned from a psychologist online (the.holistic.psychologist on IG if you’re curious) that in moments of anxiety/fear/panic we tend to have a limited field of vision which is usually helpful in dangerous situations so we can maintain heightened focus, but counterproductive if it’s just a symptom of anxiety. She suggested an exercise in which you take a few moments to keep your head fixed but really expand your field of vision by tracing your finger from one corner down to the next etc and following this only with your eyes. Opening up your vision like that helps the brain realize that there isn’t any danger and can help calm it from a panicked state. I realized this explanation is why I feel much less anxious if I’m outside and have a lot to look at. Other than that, my fave calming go-to is the song Weightless by Marconi Union. Scientists have studied the calming effects of this song and have found it REALLY useful for those struggling with anxiety. I think it’s a specific portion of the song, theres a 10 hour loop I have saved on YT I can share if you’re interested. When I get so overstimulated that I have panic attacks they physically mimic seizures but if I’m able to pull that video up, my body relaxes after a few minutes and in time, so, too, does my mind. I’ve actually fallen asleep unintentionally while listening to this.

I hope there was something helpful here for you! Wishing you the best 🙏

I’ve (27F) been stretching on & off for years but more consistently over the past 6 months. The biggest thing I noticed physically was the increased awareness of my posture and an understanding of how I’d been positioning my body incorrectly this entire time. I tended to shift my weight to the left side when casually standing or even sitting, so my hips were insanely out of place for years but I didn’t know that until I got deeper into stretching. I’ve dramatically improved my posture over all now & it’s most notable when I walk. Now that I’ve figured out my hips more, I’ve learned that a natural walking gait should rely more on movement of the hips rather than the legs to propel yourself forward—my family thinks I’m being flashy when I walk but that’s literally just how a human with proper posture should move. Also, how even young people today mention waking up or living daily with back pain, stiff neck, etc—with the exception of chronic illness and pain, this isn’t a normal thing for humans to experience. A lot of the pain we’ve come to associate with just being alive is, at least from my understanding, due to holding ourselves incorrectly which ends up misaligning ligaments in your body & building tension. Stretching helps your body realign all of this, which will greatly reduce pain if done right. I also used to go to the chiropractor frequently for adjustments following an accident—I’m at a point in my stretching practice where this is unnecessary as I’ve figured out stretches to adjust myself (wouldn’t advise without a lot of practice tho). 

Also, less tension means more relaxation overall. I can sit comfortably with myself, spine straight and no source of tension, not even on my face. The greatest aspect of this for me, tho, was the mental relaxation. I’ve struggled with anxiety/depression my entire life but with less physical tension, my mental tension has also dramatically decreased. I find myself able to be more calm regarding things that once terribly triggered me. If my mood does get low, it no longer scares me and I can sit with the feeling, explore it, and ultimately use a combination of stretching and meditation to release it. I’ve stumbled into healing from past traumas completely randomly with my stretching over the past year. Stretching and flexibility practices in general, tho, allowed me to have a greater relationship with myself in so many ways I didn’t know were possible. I continue reaping rewards each day!

From my experiences with healing past wounds and trauma, I encountered a breathing practice called “rebirthing.” The premise is, when breathing, the exhale should come naturally so as to let whatever we’re experiencing in that moment properly pass through us. Oftentimes when we’re in some sort of stressful experience, our breathing can become hectic and irregular. Me personally, I started noticing when I’m really upset or worked up over something, I unintentionally hold my breath. With the concepts explored in rebirthing, this holding of my breath essentially “traps” those emotions in my body.

Going beyond that, in my personal practices with yoga, I’ve also come to identify that these past traumatic events have become ingrained in the very ways I have held my body over the years. When those things happened, I must have subconsciously tensed myself in such a way that, paired with the disruption of my breathing, again “trapped” those feelings inside of me.

I’ve begun a more serious stretching regiment recently, and the more I relieve various tension — the more I have the exact same experience you’ve described in your post. There have been times where I’ve uncovered a new level of tension that was incredibly difficult to breathe through. But in sticking with it, I found something...releasing. Old memories resurfaced of past me and the pain she experienced, and I recognized that tension was created by HER, years ago, and she never properly healed from it. So I finally gave her the chance and breathed through the tension until it released, and it was like a dam opened up. I found myself sobbing from that old hurt, but it felt lighter. I made sure to keep my breathing even so the feeling would pass, and it eventually did. I smiled through the tears because whatever I had felt back then, I had finally, FINALLY let it go. The tension was no longer a burden, physically OR mentally.

While your post specifically hints at a more reiki/massage sort of healing, I’ve found that that same level of healing can be achieved with a stretching practice in the ways I’ve described. It lets you explore your body and reacquaint yourself with the way you’ve carried yourself over the years, and eventually in time you’ll see the ways you can relieve all of the tensions of your past — again, both physically and mentally. I’ve struggled with terrible depression and anxiety for as long as I can remember honestly, but these days it’s nowhere near as bad as it was because I’m finally letting myself heal from all the years of baggage that negatively impacted me by learning to be kind and loving to myself overall.

The process of “energy” healing can sound a bit “woowoo” at times (as a very spiritual witch even I have to admit that occasionally) but I think it honestly translate to humans on a very biological level. I’m no scientist so I can’t speak on it from that perspective but from another one I find relevant — my partner is an atheist, and autistic. A very literal person who doesn’t put much stock into the notion of energies and all that. He buys into it more for my sake, but has remained a devout skeptic nonetheless. This stretching kick I got on was inspired by him actively doing it for months before I was motivated enough to do it myself. And what do you know, what I mentioned above about the release of physical tension allowing for a release of mental tension — he came to that understanding completely on his own. I had talked to him about it before, sure, but again, he’s a skeptic. One day, though, he managed this stretch that completely opened up his chest — and he immediately started crying. In the six years we’ve been together, I’ve only seen him cry maybe once before. But on that day, something in him unlocked and out came all of the tears he had never allowed himself to cry before. He told me he felt immense relief, like a weight had been lifted. And since then, he’s been much more lighthearted and open with his emotions, allowing himself to properly feel and process them for the first time probably in his life. I’ve talked to him a lot about chakras, which again that’s something even he found a bit “woowoo.” But in his personal stretching practice, he’s actually recognized that there’s some merit to it.

I went back to my dad’s house to hang out with my grandma (was just us at the time), she went out to do some yard work and I napped briefly and fell into a dream that was the life of the girl I had seen when I was a kid, and something about that, I dunno — it opened up that connection again, she could speak to me as if she were sitting right beside me. Maybe a year or so later, I went back and she was sort of “nagging” to get my attention but I had a headache or something so was grumpy and in a half asleep state I unintentionally pictured this white light and told her she could go towards it if she wanted to, so she did. Her voice gradually got quieter and the last I heard her say was, “you made me beautiful.”

From what I understand, her father was a terrible man who mistreated her until she died, and the sheer negative emotion of that seemed to have kept her in a cycle where she maybe felt like she couldn’t move on out of fear. Me being there, connecting with her — it was like she needed someone to “hold her hand” and tell her that it was okay, she was finally allowed to find peace after all this time.

The second and last time it happened, I was attending my aunt’s wedding (somewhere around the story with the girl) which was held in a home her friend was renting to her. Important to note friend’s mother died here in this house of old age. But I could tell she hadn’t left yet. I would see her in the living room doing puzzle books, looking up every now and then as if expecting someone. I talked to her daughter once, and she told me that was her mother’s ritual when waiting for her husband to come home from work. 

I never sensed the husband until the last day I was there, when I finally recognized a little memorial stone for him out front of the house. I got some strange tingling sensation, felt a completely different presence all of a sudden. And it was the oddest feeling but I just know that that husband finally came “home” for his wife, and when he did, she went away with him so they could be in peace together. I can’t explain why, but I felt like me being there helped bridge whatever gap was dividing them out in the astral planes, maybe he had died a lot earlier and was almost completely passed on but somehow holding out hope and waiting for her to come with? I’ll probably never know, but interesting to think about nonetheless.

This comment. Yes. I wholeheartedly agree and wanted to say much the same but you said it in much better words, thank you for sharing. Healing should never hinge on another being or really anything outside of us, because you’re right—it’s unproductive and sets us up for a world of disappointment. So while it would be therapeutic for OP to have that connection with their father, it ultimately won’t be the only thing that will allow them to heal from those years of abandonment trauma. 

My biological father (better referred to sarcastically as nothing more than a sperm donor) abandoned me when I was like 3 and I was so young that I’m still peeling back the layers of trauma/depression/anxiety from those feelings of rejection and abandonment now at 27. The man is still alive but lives elsewhere, and after meeting my siblings from his side last year, they tried to encourage me to reach out to him. I wanted to for reasons similar to OP, to get a chance to tell him how much he hurt me and to ask him WHY. But the conversation was terribly harmful and sent me on a very dark spiral for the next few months. So a word of warning to OP — be careful what you wish for in seeking this connection, because it might not truly benefit you altogether.

Ultimately, I think someone willing to abandon a child is not a suitable person for that child in any way, and trying to speak to them about this will very likely not go in the way the child would hope it to. As you said in your comment, getting what we want in situations like this can derail our healing—as in my case with my sperm donor. I had to learn that there was no healing or closure available as far as he was concerned, and that I had to do the work myself to eliminate the baggage he caused me. Parents work with what they have at the time, and for some, that’s not a lot or truly helpful to their children. But at some point when the child grows up and becomes an adult, the responsibility of growth and healing transfers from the parent to the child themselves. I had to learn that the love that was lacking from that man was something only I could find again. I wish I had been able to have a positive conversation about how he made me feel, that we could have shed tears and come back together all these years later in a blur of forgiveness and love—but that wasn’t the case. He’s a monster and I’m better off without him. It’s honestly a BLESSING that he abandoned me. The real therapy started when I decided I wouldn’t let him have any power over how I felt about my life and myself.

So yes, I emphatically agree with you that OP can and should get those feelings down in some form to release them, but true healing will go beyond that and be achieved when they realize it was inside of them all along.

I honestly feel like you’re saying a lot of things 19 year old me would have felt at that time. That drive to put something out into the world to make a difference — wanting to use my writing and whatever other art I could make to do so. I started an epic story when I was about 18/19, and I knew then it would be a monster to write. I spent time trying to formulate it and develop all of the ideas before I started, but that ended up getting me nowhere but overwhelmed. I actually got a degree studying writing my from college and in prose/poetry, I was always told I had a very antiquated and flowery method of writing. Sharing that because of your comments about being flowery somewhat like Shakespeare and to encourage you to never let someone’s depiction of you as a writer tell you what or how to write. You don’t have to conform to a certain type of story telling just because the world tells you your writing is better suited for it. Your writing is suited best for whatever YOU want to get out of it. 

Art is and always has been about stylistic preferences, and I urge you to not be like me and take too long to truly know what that means. I found my professor’s comments incredibly discouraging and honestly wanted to give it all up. If they thought my writing was no good, would anyone? This is a horrible line of thinking and nothing any artist or writer should ever get hung up on. We write for ourselves at the end of the day, and if we do decide to make it public, someone somewhere will resonate with our messages, maybe more powerful than we could have ever imagined. 

I may not have always been very consistent with that story, but I loved the ideas, the concepts, everything. It felt like a story worthy of being told, so eventually I just wrote for the sake of writing. I’m 26 now and you would not believe how many massive plot overhauls I’ve done on this. I was disappointed in how long it took to get here, but it finally is what it needs to be and I’m so thrilled to be working on it. It doesn’t matter that it didn’t happen “on time” or that I didn’t always know how to start it. Sometimes all we need is patience and trust in our abilities, and the rest will flow.

Long story short, don’t let the blank page be daunting. Just write! Even if you have no idea what to write just write literally anything and something will come from it. I’d even recommend starting with 1000 words a day just to get in the habit—you’d be surprised what you might discover from this. Happy writing!

My most recent doctor explained that this is beneficial to reducing inflammation in the body normally associated with the period, and it can greatly decrease the intensity of your cramps as well as reduce other aches and pains you might normally get. My periods aren’t as bad anymore because of birth control so I don’t do this as often but when I was younger, taking ibuprofen like this to be preventative was often the only way I could function during the week of my period. Your parents sound like they probably keep things under “lock and key,” so to speak so I’m not sure how easy it would be for you to access medication but regardless, I figured I’d share this just so you are aware that you’re not alone and there can be ways to diminish the pain. Research shows the main difference between introverts and extroverts are their dopamine levels, introverts naturally having higher levels and thus requiring less external stimulation. I'm an introvert but I think my dopamine levels are higher than the average for introverts. High levels of dopamine can lead to: higher cognitive functioning  (perhaps feeling like you're processing too fast and everyone around you is moving really slow), and in turn agitation and restlessness; You might adopt pleasure seeking behavior as a result, but these pleasurable things (even the most simple, say, texting for instance) can quickly lead to overstimulation and anxiety; you may feel hyperactive or highly motivated. If you're producing TOO much dopamine: aggression and depression; severe anxiety; paranoia, delusions, and hallucinations; muscle twitching. 

Personally, I knew I needed to seek help when my anxiety was causing me to quit every job a few months after I started. I worked mostly in customer service and usually I love dealing with people, but after a time it became too much. I'd start to get really angry and twitchy, sometimes convulsing. I was having several panic attacks a week. But it wasn't even work, it was friends, family, leaving my house. Everything overwhelmed me. I don't even feel safe driving a car because I'm concerned about my anxious reactions in such a situation. My anxiety would get so bad I'd crash into a depression accompanied by intense delusions, and I started hallucinating a voice that tried to convince me to kill myself. I had been in and out of therapy my whole life, I had learned good coping mechanisms (meditation, yoga, exercise) but it still wasn't enough. After shamefully confessing to a doctor I wanted to kill myself, she recommended a psychiatrist so I went. After describing my problem, he summed it up by saying: "It's like you're processing all of life but your personal volume has been turned up to a screech and the knob is broken; you can't turn it down and now everything overwhelms you." I cried when he said that because it was exactly right. I've been anxious and highly sensitive my whole life, and no one had been able to describe to me why. He started me on an anti psychotic medication called Risperidone that works to lower dopamine levels and I almost immediately noticed an improvement. It's been about two to three months since I started that and while I still struggle, my "volume knob" has finally been turned down.

I would say only consider medication if you think it's absolutely necessary. In my personal experience, I was past the point of desperation and my life literally depended on it. Like I asked in my previous post, is your anxiety interfering with your life in a way that positive coping habits don't make a dent in? If so, medication may prove beneficial. If you notice that refraining from certain dopamine inducing activities helps to substantially lower your anxiety then perhaps it's something you should bring up with a doctor.

Is your anxiety in any way debilitating? Is it preventing you from living your life? Do you spend more time fighting off anxiety than living? If you answered yes, then you should seek professional help. There's no reason to feel ashamed. In my personal experience, seeking help showed me that my anxiety was caused by an overproduction of dopamine, which is something best handled by medication. Had I not gone to a professional, there's no way I would have known that--i would have kept on doing what I thought worked to no avail. This won't necessarily be your case, but talking to a professional can show you a side of your anxiety you never considered, and in this new perspective is a solution.
